title: Skipping fixed action fields
statement: Let $x$ be a binary input, and let a base configuration, destination, bounded counter, binary table, state tape, and state-tape cursor be given. For every nonnegative integer $n$, field index $f\in\{0,\ldots,7\}$, and table cursor $p$, if $f+n=7$, then starting in the fixed-field-skipping phase at field $f$ and cursor $p$, after $n+1$ steps the stopped interpreter is in the unary-tail-scanning phase with the same destination and remaining counter, table cursor $p+n+1$, and unchanged state tape and state-tape cursor.
hypotheses_covered: A base configuration, destination, bounded counter, binary table, state tape, and state-tape cursor
A field index $f\in\{0,\ldots,7\}$ and table cursor $p$
replaced:
In the fixed-field-skipping phase of the stopped table interpreter, with
current field index $i$ and $n$ further fields remaining (so $i + n = 7$),
exactly $n+1$ steps advance the table cursor by $n+1$ cells and enter the
unary-tail scanner; no tape content is inspected or modified.
